SEDarc Studentship Competition 2027-2028

The South East Doctoral Training Arc (SEDarc) is pleased to offer Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) funding for PhD students for September 2027 entry.

About SEDarc

SEDarc is a consortium of six universities: Kingston University, Royal Holloway University of London, University of Kent, University of Reading, University of Surrey, and University of Sussex. It offers funding for doctoral studentships, supporting postgraduate researchers in undertaking impactful doctoral research and training. Three studentships are ring-fenced for applicants who meet our widening participation criteria, as part of our commitment to equity and inclusion.

Studentship Offer

  • Full details of the studentship offer, award structures, and assessment criteria are available on the SEDarc website.
  • The PhDs are open to UK and international students and consist of UK home fees and stipend awards.
  • Part-time study is available, but due to visa restrictions, this option is only available to those with home fee status.
  • Deferred start dates are not possible.
  • Applicants who have already commenced a PhD are not eligible.

How to Apply

Students must be nominated by one of the six SEDarc institutions to apply to the doctoral programme. Please contact one of the Administrators at the SEDarc institution of your choice, as each institution has a different deadline and process for the institutional stage of the application process. The deadline for applications to SEDarc is 29 January 2027 at 16:00 (GMT).

Contact Administrators

  • Kingston University: hssce-research@kingston.ac.uk
  • Royal Holloway, University of London: esrcdtp@rhul.ac.uk
  • University of Kent: kentgrc@kent.ac.uk
  • University of Reading: doctoralstudentshipsofficer@reading.ac.uk
  • University of Surrey: doctoralcollege@surrey.ac.uk
  • University of Sussex: pgr-scholarships@sussex.ac.uk

Assessment and Steer Groups

SEDarc is committed to identifying and awarding high quality applications and projects within our panel review process under three specific steer groups:

  • Advanced Data Skills
  • Advanced Quantitative Methods
  • Interdisciplinary Collaboration with researchers outside of the social sciences

Please speak to your selected institution should your project include any of the above to ensure these are highlighted within your application.

Ring-Fenced Studentships

SEDarc ring-fences up to 3 studentships for home students who meet the following:

  • Be assessed as being eligible to pay fees at the home fee rate
  • Identify as being of one of the following ethnic groups: Black or Black British – Caribbean; Black or Black British - African; Other Black background; Asian or Asian British - Bangladeshi; Asian or Asian British – Pakistani; Asian or Asian British - Indian
  • Meet all other eligibility criteria

Frequently Asked Questions

  • You are only permitted to submit ONE application for a SEDarc studentship.
  • SEDarc cannot assist with finding a supervisor; contact your chosen university.
  • Part-time study is available only for home fee status.
  • Deferrals are not possible.
  • Applicants who have already started a PhD are not eligible.
  • Assessment criteria are available on the SEDarc website.
  • The stipend tax liability should be checked with HMRC.
  • Individual feedback is not provided due to high volume.
  • Reserve list outcomes are matched based on fee status and research focus.

Note

ESRC DTPs are subject to a mid-term review in 2026, and studentship numbers may be revised based on the review findings. Allocations for the 2027 cohort are expected to be confirmed around January 2027.

2026/27 UKRI reference rate: the minimum UKRI doctoral stipend is £21,805 per year, tax-free (London institutions +£2,000), effective 1 October 2026.
